summary:
The agent played three episodes, about 290 s of game time in all: episode 1 (60 s), episode 2 (game time 74–245 s, a full 150 s round, the "Time!" screen and a second round started with "Skate again"), and episode 3 (60 s, continuing that second round). Jev made 219, 871 and 156 decisions, choosing among 6–9 options each time. Every option was named and worded in the terms the bottom-left controls line uses. Jev was given only what a new player sees: the HUD and goal-line texts, the controls line, the minimap icons, the glowing goal ring, and the skatepark features once within about 45 m.

**First times (episode 2 is the clean round; its round started at game time 74.3 s with the timer at 2:30):**
- **First push:** about 1 s into the round. In episode 1 it was 0.5 s.
- **First jump:** about 8 s into the round, at the skatepark ("Hop", 50 points). In episode 1 it was 5.9 s.
- **First grind snap:** only in episode 1, at 30.4 s, near the park's 3 m round rail. It fell off 0.17 s later. A second snap, onto the 6 m concrete ledge at about 41 s, also ended in a fall at 41.3 s. In episodes 2 and 3 no grind ever snapped (the run-ins missed the 3 m rail; the line-up on the 9 m bar got interrupted).
- **First 3-move combo:** 28.7 s into the round, game time 103.0 s: "Hop! + Walk It Out + Toe Spin", 385 x 3, banked +1,155. In episode 3 one came 37.1 s into the episode: "Hop + Bankhead Bounce + Toe Spin", banked +1,320.
- Later combos reached 4 moves: "Hop + Crisscross! + Hop! + Smooth Quad!" banked +2,152. Round 1 ended at 9,582 points, Silver.

**Falls off a rail:** both came right after a snap (episode 1, 30.53 s and 41.3 s). Both were most likely caused by the harness's steering, not by the game. Its balance keys at first pushed the wrong way (a background reading of the code found the A/D sign reversed), and it released F when Jev switched options. A new player would meet the same thing, though: nothing on screen says which way to lean. Only the BALANCE dot, shown while grinding, hints at it.

**The main design findings:** the screen does not teach the round's goals, and the start hint names no controls. Details and times are below.
evidence: Trace files: runs/20261113-092119/trace1.jsonl (episode 1, game time 13.3–73 s), trace2.jsonl (episode 2, game time 74.3–245.5 s), trace3.jsonl (episode 3, game time 246.3–306 s). Episode 2's run_harness call timed out in the sandbox, so it has no summary; its trace is complete to 245.5 s.

Episode 2 round start, game time 74.32: HUD shows score 0, timer 2:30 and the goal line 'Claim it: land a 2,000 point combo in the skatepark'. The only text that names controls is the bottom-left line: 'WASD or arrows to skate, Space to jump, hold F to grind, Q and E to dance, R to skate backward or forward... Land moves on the beat for a bonus.'
Episode 2 at 82.57: hud-combo 'Hop', pending '50 x 1' (first jump). At 83.9: 'Hop + Bankhead Bounce', '200 x 2'. At 85.15: score 400.
Episode 2 at 102.98: hud-combo 'Hop! + Walk It Out + Toe Spin', pending '385 x 3'. At 104.15: score 1,555, '+1,155'. This is the first 3-move combo, 28.7 s into the round.
Episode 2 at 205.23–207.65: 'Hop + Crisscross! + Hop! + Smooth Quad!', '538 x 4', then '+2,152'.

Episode 2 at 224.37: the 'Time!' modal shows Score 9,582, 'Silver medal · Gold at 12,000', Best combo 2,152, and the goals 'Score 6,000 points ✓', 'Land a 1,000 point combo ✓', 'Collect 3 fact cards – 0/3', 'Freedom Parkway Underpass Hop – Not yet', 'Stone Mountain Trail Bridge Hop – Not yet'. Jev clicked 'Skate again' at 224.7; the new round started at 225.6 (timer back to 149).

Episode 1 timeline (seconds since the episode started): first push 0.51, first jump 5.85, first dance link 7.6, first grind snap 30.36. Rail falls (stats.falls going up) at 30.53 (F held, 3.6 m/s, near the 3 m round rail) and 41.3 (just after snapping onto the 6 m concrete ledge at about 41.1). The game's exitReason read null both times (it is a one-tick flag).
Episode 3 (continuing round 2): first 3-move combo at 37.08 s: ['Hop', 'Bankhead Bounce', 'Toe Spin'], pending 440, banked +1,320 by 39.9. No grind snap in that episode.

Goal line changes in episode 1: 'Claim it: hop under the Freedom Parkway bridge' from 0 to about 11 s; 'Claim it: ride the 3 rings in order in 24 s' at 12.2 s; 'Claim it: land a 2,000 point combo in the skatepark' at 23.3 s; back to 'ride the 3 rings' at 59.3 s. The line flips as the player moves.

Episode 2 ring attempt: 'Ring 2 of 3: 24 s left' at 178.4, counting down to 9 s at 196.4, then back to '24 s left' at 197.7 and again at 217.15 without any message. Ring 3 was never reached before time ran out.

Episode 2, after 'Skate again' (game time 226–245.5): speed 0 for about 20 s while skate_to_skatepark_icon ran. Episode 3, seconds 4.6–25.4: speed 0.0 with the skatepark icon 'ahead'. Frames of episode 3 at game times 249–273 show the skater standing idle (hand on hip) on open grass with nothing in front, the camera drifting. It moved again at 26.6 s, after the option restarted and pressed W anew.

Frames of episode 3 (game times 249–273) show no HUD, goal line or minimap: the HUD is page markup over the canvas and is not in the filmed frames. All on-screen text comes from game.screen() in the traces.
Game error log: no errors logged in episodes 1 and 3. Episode 2's summary was lost to the sandbox timeout.
findings: Design: the start hint 'Press any key or click to start the beat' disappears on the first key and names no control. The only control help is the small bottom-left info line. The words 'push' and 'brake' never appear: W pushes and S brakes only as part of 'WASD to skate'. Carving, braking and the R switch go untaught.

Design: the HUD never explains the round's goals. Score 6,000, a 1,000-point combo, 3 fact cards and two gap hops are shown only on the 'Time!' screen at the end (episode 2, 224.37). In episode 2 the agent met the 1,000-combo goal at about 104 s (+1,155) and passed 6,000 points at about 207 s with no sign on screen. It learned of the fact cards and the bridge hops only after the round, when the goals read 'Not yet'.

Design: the one goal line ('Claim it: ...') is about landmark claims, not the round goals. It switches with distance between 'hop under the Freedom Parkway bridge', 'ride the 3 rings in order in 24 s' and 'land a 2,000 point combo in the skatepark' (episode 1 at 0, 12.2, 23.3 and 59.3 s). By the code (not checked in play), claims don't add to the HUD score either, so a player who completes one sees no reward.

Unclear moment (episode 2, 178–224 s): the goal line read 'Ring 2 of 3: N s left' but jumped back to '24 s left' twice (197.7, 217.15) with no message, while the agent was skating rings 1–2. The screen does not say the attempt restarted, or why (by the code: re-entering ring 1).

Unclear moment / possible input issue: after 'Skate again', the skater stood still for about 20 s with the push key held (episode 2, 226–245; episode 3, 4.6–25.4). The frames show an idle pose on open grass with nothing in front. It moved again only after the keys were released and pressed again. Whether the game drops a key held across the results modal or the harness's hold went stale is not settled. The development team should check whether a key held through the 'Time!' modal is ignored afterwards.

Design: dances (Q/E) do nothing in the air or on a rail, and a move's combo link appears only when the dance ends (0.6–1.2 s later). The agent's first chain attempt, dancing in the air, gave only 2 links (episode 1, 5.7–8.4 s). The screen says only 'Q and E to dance'. A new player trying to chain 'Hop' with a dance in the air gets nothing, with no feedback why.

Design/feel: grinds are hard to find and keep. Rails are only in the skatepark, which only the minimap's skate icon points to, 73 m from spawn. The 3 m round rail met first from spawn missed on every run-in. The two snaps (episode 1, 30.36 and about 41.1) both fell within 0.2 s. The only lean guidance is the BALANCE dot, shown only while grinding.

Spawn sits about 20 m from the Freedom Parkway bridge spot: a first hop there may count for the 'Underpass Hop' goal, but nothing on screen says so (not observed in play: in round 1 the agent never jumped there, and the goal read 'Not yet').

Harness limits (not game bugs): Jev's 'is it clear what to do next' question failed validation in all three episodes, so unclear moments come from the traces, not from Jev's own judgment. The game ran about 3x slower than wall time, which cut episode 2's summary short.
prompt: Playtest the BeltLine Eastside level as a first-time player who has never seen the game, for about 3 minutes of play. Use only what the screen teaches: the start hint, the HUD, the prompts and the map. Do not use knowledge from the code to find moves the screen does not show. Try to push, carve, brake, jump, grind and do a style move, and try to chain 3 moves into one combo. Report: the game time of the first push, the first jump, the first grind snap and the first 3-move combo (or that it never happened); each time the player falls off a rail by accident; each moment the player does not know what to do next, and what was on the screen then; whether the HUD and hints explain the goals. The 150 s round may end: start a new round and continue. This is a design evaluation: report what a new player meets, with times and frames, not only bugs.
